key_insight: TerMeZO fine-tunes BitNet LLMs with zeroth-order optimization by selecting only the latent weights most likely to change under ternary quantization, reducing memory while preserving performance.
engineering_relevance: This enables edge-friendly adaptation of BitNet models with a memory footprint closer to inference-time use, making large-model fine-tuning more practical on constrained hardware.
method: Uses MeZO-style forward-pass-only optimization to avoid gradient storage.
Exploits ternary quantizer geometry to identify sparse latent-weight updates without extra data or first-order gradients.
Reduces the effective fine-tuning dimension to improve speed and memory efficiency.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates BitNet models from 1B to 3B parameters across classification, instruction-following, and mathematical reasoning tasks, reporting that TerMeZO matches or exceeds full-parameter MeZO.
watch_item: Sparse update selection depends on the quantizer geometry and latent-weight dynamics, so performance may be sensitive to model scale and task-specific quantization behavior.
paper_title: TerMeZO: Ternary Sparse Zeroth-Order Optimization for Fine-tuning BitNet Models at the Edge
